note: phase K — declare a `type struct`, construct via a pinned literal, read fields, whole-value reassign
phase K — `type Position = Vec3;` is a transparent alias; values interchange freely
phase K — `type struct Dog = { ...Animal, goodBoy: bool };` merges Animal's fields with the new field (through an alias operand)
phase K — `type struct Cat = Animal & { color: int32 };` intersection composition mirrors spread
phase K — a `Vec3 { ... }` literal is self-typed and checks against the `const v: Vec3` annotation
phase K — a `Vec3 { ... }` literal checks against the declared parameter type at the call site
phase K — a `Vec3 { ... }` literal checks against the enclosing function's declared return type
phase K — a self-typed `Vec3 { ... }` literal needs no annotation; the binding type is inferred from it
phase K — an object literal naming an undeclared type (`Bogus { ... }`) is rejected
phase K — coverage check: literal omits a field declared on the target struct
phase K — coverage check: literal introduces a field not declared on the target struct
phase K — coverage check: a field name appears twice in the literal
phase K — `v.field` member-access reads on a struct-typed binding

phase K — partial init via `v.field = ...;` before whole-value assignment is rejected
phase K — `{ ...a }` value-spread of the same struct type covers every field

phase K — a spread + explicit field naming the same slot is a collision
phase K — two operands of a composition declare the same field name
phase K — composition operands must be struct types; `int32 & { ... }` is rejected
phase K — mutual composition cycle `A = { ...B }; B = { ...A }` is rejected
phase K — direct self-reference (`Tree.left: Tree`) cannot be broken without `heap T`
phase K — mutual inline-field cycle `A.b: B; B.a: A;` is rejected
phase K — `==` / `!=` on struct operands is rejected; struct equality would synthesize hidden fieldwise control flow
phase K — `<` / `>` / `<=` / `>=` on struct operands is rejected (§8.9)

phase K — a function returns a struct alias that stays compatible with the underlying struct type
phase K — a struct-returning function rejects a primitive return value
phase K — a function directly returns a struct literal pinned by its declared return type
phase K — a function return annotation can pin a struct literal through an alias
phase K — a returned struct literal must initialize every field required by the return type
phase K — returned struct literals match fields by name, allow source reordering, and allow a trailing comma
phase K — a function can return an empty literal pinned to an empty struct type
phase K — a return-context literal can construct a struct produced by composition
phase K — the outer return type and struct field types pin nested struct literals
phase K — a returned struct literal accepts a complete same-type value spread
phase K — a returned struct literal rejects fields absent from the declared return type
phase K — a returned struct literal rejects an explicitly repeated field
phase K — each returned struct literal field value must match the field type supplied by context
phase K — a returned struct literal rejects a spread whose field names match but field types differ (int32 vs float64)
phase K — a returned struct literal rejects a field supplied both by spread and explicitly
phase K — nested struct literals pinned through return context enforce complete field coverage
phase K — methods inside `type struct { ... }` are a parser error (§8.5); any error accepted
phase K — per-field `public` / `private` inside `type struct { ... }` is a parser error (§8.5); any error accepted
phase K — per-field default initializers inside `type struct { ... }` are a parser error (§8.11); any error accepted
